account:
Today appears routine so far, despite my feeling that something might be happening without me. During my morning market walk, three townsfolk each said they had no news. I have seen no evidence of a secret gathering or unusual trade.

The secretary's mention of two appointment books briefly seemed unusual. She explained that she wrote a provisional office record while I had the original, recording my market walk and unconfirmed appointments rather than a different schedule. I have not read that second book myself, but her explanation fits what happened this morning.

The original book left the host and address of my three o'clock tea unclear. The secretary went to the east-bank dockside cottages to confirm it. I found her with neighbour at the cottage by (16, -60, 105), and heard neighbour confirm that he expects me there at three. This appears to be an ordinary tea appointment, not evidence of another undertaking.

I am now home, at 12:36, for my scheduled lunch. Accounts at the office are due at one, tea at three, and another office engagement at four-thirty. I still want to learn more about town affairs, but nothing I have heard today establishes that anyone is concealing business from me.
